title: Open-adjunction normalization of proper/open interchange on strict coefficient towers
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] such that every $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
U&\xrightarrow{k}&V\\
r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
W&\xrightarrow{i}&Z
\end{array}$$
be a commutative square of Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], meaning $pk=ir$, with $r,p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $i,k$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]; cartesianness is not assumed. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and constant $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every corner $T$ put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ [def-weil-inverse-system], and use its unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], equivalently the ringed diagram-site derived category of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Write $G_u=u^{-1}$ termwise for inverse image and $R_u^{\mathcal T}$ for the total derived termwise direct image, with the canonical adjunction $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. For an open immersion $j$, write $J_j$ for termwise extension by zero: sheafify the presheaf which takes an object factoring through the open to the given module's sections there, and takes any other object to zero, with the corresponding restriction maps. Sheafification means the left adjoint to inclusion of sheaves [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This defines an exact functor on module diagrams and hence on their derived categories; its canonical adjunction is $J_j\dashv G_j$, with unit the identity identification $G_jJ_j\cong1$.

There is a canonical natural open-restriction isomorphism
$$\lambda_Q:G_iR_p^{\mathcal T}J_k\xrightarrow{\sim}R_r^{\mathcal T},$$
obtained by restricting $p$ to $V_W=V\times_Z W$, then factoring $k$ through its open-and-closed image $U\to V_W$, and using extension by zero on that open-and-closed component. The induced map $U\to V_W$ is an open-and-closed immersion. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its direct-image comparison uses K-injective diagram resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; its restriction to a Cartesian square is the inverse-image/direct-image square mate for base change by $i$, followed by the open unit identification. In the general commutative case it uses the same open restriction and the direct-image composition for the open-and-closed component. Define $\Gamma_Q:J_iR_r^{\mathcal T}\to R_p^{\mathcal T}J_k$ as the adjunct under $J_i\dashv G_i$ of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$, so
$$\lambda_Q\circ G_i\Gamma_Q=1_{R_r^{\mathcal T}}$$
under the open unit identification. This specifies an actual morphism in the derived diagram category, not a family of levelwise arrows.

Let $N\in D(\mathcal T_U)$ and suppose that for each $n$ its evaluation has a specified isomorphism
$$N_n\simeq\operatorname{Res}_{\underline A\to\underline{P_n}}\nu_U^*L_n,\qquad L_n\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},P_n),$$
where $\nu_U$ is the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the isomorphism is an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and restriction of scalars is termwise [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. No transitions between the $L_n$ are assumed; $N$ already carries its strict transitions. Then $\Gamma_{Q,N}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal T_Z)$. Evaluating it at $n$ and using the canonical direct-image and scalar-restriction comparisons gives the restriction of the pro-etale transport of the specified finite proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], with direction $i_!Rr_*\to Rp_*k_!$. This statement fixes the comparison by its open adjunction and asserts its finite evaluation normalization; no faithfulness of evaluation functors on derived morphisms is asserted.

proof.text: Identify the operations with the existing strict constant-coefficient tower operations, taking $B=A$ and reindexing $n\geq1$ as $n-1\in\mathbb N$. The localized-site equivalence identifies the coefficient ring with $\underline A$ on the open, preserving constant sections. In the extension-by-zero presheaf of the module adjunction, the summands at a test object $H$ are indexed by maps $H\to U$ over the ambient scheme. There is at most one such map, and it exists precisely when $H$ factors through the open. Thus that presheaf is exactly the presheaf in the statement, not a different version of extension by zero. Its restriction to the open is the original sheaf, so the adjunction unit is the indicated identification. Exactness and the induced derived adjunction are those of the cited open-extension operation. The quasi-compactness hypothesis in the strict-tower calculus holds: the inverse image of an affine open under $i$ or $k$ is an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme, hence quasi-compact by the cited Noetherian-open lemma. Apply the calculus to this square. It supplies $S=V\times_ZW$, $b:S\hookrightarrow V$, $q:S\to W$, and the clopen lift $s:U\hookrightarrow S$, with $bs=k$, $qs=r$. It also supplies a comparison $\gamma_Q:J_iR_r^{\mathcal T}\to R_p^{\mathcal T}J_k$, defined as the proper-adjunction mate of $\alpha_Q=(J_b\pi_sG_q)\beta_{i,p}$. In the following steps we identify this specific comparison with the one specified in the item.

source.place: Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero); the module construction is sites-modules.tex Section 03DH and Tag 03DJ; agent identification with the strict-tower calculus

proof.text: For the clopen $s$, put $S'=S\setminus s(U)$. Every test object $H\to S$ is covered by its disjoint inverse images in $s(U)$ and $S'$. A module sheaf is therefore uniquely specified by its two restrictions: sections on $H$ are the product of the sections on those two opens, and gluing gives the inverse to restriction. This applies to maps, transitions, and differentials as well. In this product description $G_s$ is projection onto the first factor and both $J_s$ and $s_*$ are $F\mapsto(F,0)$. They are canonically identified by the map which is identity on $U$ and zero on $S'$. In particular $s_*$ is exact and $J_s=R_s^{\mathcal T}$ after deriving. The direct-image adjunction unit $1\to R_s^{\mathcal T}G_s$ is exactly the clopen projection $\pi_s$ of the calculus. Open-extension composition gives $G_bJ_k=G_bJ_bJ_s=J_s$, with all identifications preserving the open units. No proper base-change theorem or finiteness of coefficients is used in this decomposition.

proof.text:
Work on the small ringed diagram sites realizing the tower categories. They have K-injective resolutions. The ringed-site localization comparison gives the sectionwise identity $G_i p_*\cong q_*G_b$ before deriving. Restriction $G_b$ preserves K-injectives because it is right adjoint to the exact $J_b$. Consequently, if $F\to I$ is a K-injective diagram resolution, both $G_iR_p^{\mathcal T}F$ and $R_q^{\mathcal T}G_bF$ are represented by the identical complex $q_*G_bI$. This constructs a natural isomorphism $\chi:G_iR_p^{\mathcal T}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_q^{\mathcal T}G_b$, normalized by the identity on restricted sections. It is the inverse-image/direct-image square mate: the sectionwise identity is the transpose of the restricted direct-image counit, and deriving the same adjunctions preserves this description. With the clopen identification of step 2 and the canonical derived direct-image composition comparison, form
$$\lambda_Q:G_iR_p^{\mathcal T}J_k\xrightarrow{\chi J_k}R_q^{\mathcal T}G_bJ_k\cong R_q^{\mathcal T}J_s\cong R_q^{\mathcal T}R_s^{\mathcal T}\cong R_r^{\mathcal T}.$$
These operations occur on the diagram sites, so this is a natural isomorphism of functors on the entire derived tower category. When the original square is cartesian, $s=1$ and this formula is precisely the open base-change mate followed by $G_kJ_k=1$.

proof.text:
We compute the open adjunct of $\gamma_Q$, suppressing the normalized composition isomorphisms. Write $R_u=R_u^{\mathcal T}$, and write $\eta_u,\varepsilon_u$ for $G_u\dashv R_u$. By the mate formula,
$$\gamma_Q=R_pJ_k\varepsilon_r\circ R_p\alpha_QR_r\circ\eta_pJ_iR_r.$$
Let $\theta:G_bG_p\xrightarrow{\sim}G_qG_i$ be the localized inverse-image identification. The mate formula for the sectionwise comparison $\chi:G_iR_p\to R_qG_b$ gives the typed unit equation
$$R_q\theta\circ\chi G_p\circ G_i\eta_p=\eta_qG_i.$$
This follows by substituting the mate formula and canceling the $G_p\dashv R_p$ unit-counit pair. Apply this equation at $J_iR_rN$ and identify $G_iJ_iR_rN=R_rN$. The restriction of $\beta_{i,p}$, after $G_bJ_b=1$ and $G_iJ_i=1$, is the identity of $G_qR_rN$: indeed its inverse has precisely the open-unit transpose specified by the calculus, and that unit becomes the identity after these identifications. Thus restricting $\alpha_Q=(J_b\pi_sG_q)\beta_{i,p}$ leaves $\pi_sG_q$, with no residual automorphism. Naturality of $\chi$ moves $R_pJ_k\varepsilon_r$ through the restriction comparison. Inserting these three equalities into the mate formula gives
$$\lambda_Q\,G_i\gamma_Q
=R_qJ_s\varepsilon_r\circ R_q\pi_sG_qR_r\circ\eta_qR_r.$$
Here $R_qJ_s=R_r$ by step 2. Moreover $\pi_s=\eta_s$ under $J_s=R_s$. The composite-adjunction unit for $G_r=G_sG_q\dashv R_qR_s=R_r$ is
$$\eta_r=R_q\eta_sG_q\circ\eta_q.$$
Substitution therefore gives
$$\lambda_Q\,G_i\gamma_Q=R_r\varepsilon_r\circ\eta_rR_r=1_{R_r},$$
by the adjunction triangle identity. The computation uses transformations in the derived tower categories and their normalized units, rather than an equality tested after evaluation. Thus $G_i\gamma_Q=\lambda_Q^{-1}$. The bijection for $J_i\dashv G_i$, whose unit is the open identification, says that $\gamma_Q$ is exactly the adjunct defining $\Gamma_Q$. This proves both existence of the specified actual morphism and its normalization.

proof.text: Apply the finite-origin and finite-evaluation clauses of the strict-tower calculus to $B=A$, the homomorphisms $A\to P_n=A/I^n$, and the given isomorphisms $N_n\simeq\operatorname{Res}\nu_U^*L_n$. Each $P_n$ is a finite commutative ring and each $L_n$ is bounded below, exactly as required there. The calculus permits a different bound and finite coefficient ring at each $n$; it requires no system of transitions between the $L_n$. Its strict tower input is $N$ itself. It follows that $\gamma_{Q,N}$ is invertible and that its $n$-th evaluation, through the canonical scalar and site direct-image/open-extension comparisons, is the normalized finite proper/open map of the cited finite-coherence node, directed $i_!Rr_*\to Rp_*k_!$. Since step 4 proves $\Gamma_Q=\gamma_Q$ before evaluating, these assertions hold for the specific $\Gamma_{Q,N}$ in the item. No injectivity of evaluation on morphisms is used.
